entries.raw: Today I came down that escalator at Trump Tower. Thousands of people inside, friends, families, press. I announced I was running for President. They didn't think I'd do it. I said we need to make America great again. The crowds went wild. It was tremendous.

levels.sentence: I came down that escalator, thousands of people, and I said I'm running for President — we're going to make America great again, and they loved it, believe me.

I announced I was running for President, and honestly, they didn't think I'd do it, but I did it. I said we need to make America great again, and the crowds went wild. It was tremendous, really tremendous.
levels.summary:

I told them we need to make America great again, and the place erupted. It was something special, really special.

The energy was unbelievable. The crowds were cheering, the cameras were flashing, and I felt like we were already winning. That message — Make America Great Again — it's going to change everything. It was a tremendous day, the start of something big, believe me.

Then the other side called. The woman, very nice, very gracious.

She congratulated me. I thanked her. And then I went out and thanked my people, the greatest people. We did something that nobody thought could happen.

It was big, it was beautiful. What a night.

entries.raw: I spoke to a huge crowd on the Ellipse. I said to march peacefully, peacefully now. They went to the Capitol and it became a mess. Not what I wanted at all. But what they were doing was stealing the election. Still, I hate to see violence. We have to move forward, but they can't stop us.

I hate violence, absolutely hate it. But they are stealing the election, and that can't be allowed. We have to move forward, but they can't stop us.
levels.summary:
Look, I gave a tremendous speech on the Ellipse. Huge crowd, the biggest you've ever seen. ' That's what I said. Very important. The people were excited, they were there to protest a rigged election, a stolen election. And then what happens? They go to the Capitol, and it becomes a mess. A real mess.

Not what I wanted, not at all. I hate violence, I've always said that. But you know what? The Democrats and the fake news, they're making a big deal out of it, trying to blame me. But I want peace. I want law and order. But we can't let them steal an election, folks. We can't.

So now we have to move forward. We're going to continue to fight, we're going to win, believe me. The movement is tremendous. They can't stop us. We're going to take it all back. This was a sad day, but a day that shows how corrupt the system is. We'll never give up. We'll never stop. And that's the truth.

entries.raw: Today I was sworn in for the second time, the 47th President. They took a picture of me raising my fist, very iconic. I spoke to a big crowd in Capitol, no nonsense. We're going to fix the border, the economy, all of it. It's going to be the best ever, you'll see.

levels.sentence: Today I got sworn in for the second time—47th President—and I raised my fist for the camera, spoke to a massive crowd at the Capitol, and promised to fix the border and the economy like nobody's ever seen.
levels.paragraph: Today was big. Tremendous, really. I took the oath again, second time, 47th President. That picture of me with my fist up? Iconic, everyone loved it. I looked at that huge crowd and told them—no nonsense—we're going to fix the border, fix the economy, fix everything. Best ever, you'll see.

I spoke straight to them, no nonsense. We're going to secure the border, we're going to bring back the economy, and we're going to do it better than anybody ever did. It's going to be the best ever—believe me.

This is a movement, and we're just getting started.

memories.subject: My father, Fred Trump
memories.label: The Boss
memories.text: My father was a very powerful man, very tough. He built thousands of apartments in Brooklyn and Queens. He taught me that this business is about the site, the land, and getting the damn thing done. He was proud of me, even when he didn't say it. I miss him.

levels.sentence: My father, Fred Trump, was a tough, powerful man who built thousands of apartments in Brooklyn and Queens, taught me everything about the business, and I miss him a lot, believe me.
levels.paragraph: My father, Fred Trump, was a very powerful man, very tough, believe me. He built thousands of apartments across Brooklyn and Queens — tremendous number, like nobody's ever seen. He taught me everything: the site, the land, getting the damn thing done. He was proud of me, even if he didn't always say it. I miss him, I really do.
levels.summary:
My father, Fred Trump, was something special — a self-made man, a tremendous builder. He put up thousands of apartments in Brooklyn and Queens, and I mean thousands — the best buildings, the finest locations, nobody did it better. He was tough as nails.

He didn't hand you anything; he taught you the real deal: the site, the land, and getting the damn thing done. That's the business. That's the whole ballgame.

He was proud of me, even when he didn't say it. I knew it. I felt it. A lot of people talk about their fathers, but I had the best. When I think about him, I think about those lessons, and I miss him, I really do. But he'd want me to keep building, keep winning. And I do.

I turned it around, and I learned that there are sharks everywhere. But I'm the biggest shark, the biggest and the best. Believe me.

We were five children, and she always believed in me. I got my drive from her, no question. I grew up in Jamaica Estates, Queens, a tough kid, a great athlete.

At thirteen, my parents sent me to New York Military Academy, and that taught me discipline — real discipline. That's where it all started.

And my children? All special. Don Jr. and Eric run the company — fantastic job, great leaders. Ivanka was in the White House — tremendous job for the country. Tiffany is a lawyer — very smart, very capable. And Barron is tall, brilliant, just a great young man. I'm very proud of every one of them.

It's a great family — probably the best.

levels.paragraph: Coming to Manhattan was the beginning of everything—I was young, but I had the guts to take on the biggest deals. I grabbed Penn Central, got laughed at, then made the Commodore Hotel a tremendous win with a special city deal. That put me on the map, so I built Trump Tower—58 stories of glass and bronze, the most talked-about building anywhere. Then Atlantic City: Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, the Taj Mahal—huge, the best—but the junk bonds were a total disaster. I restructured, fought back, never quit, because I'm the biggest shark in the water.
levels.summary:
Coming to Manhattan was the beginning of everything. I was real young, but I had the guts to go after the biggest deals in the city. I took on Penn Central and their properties—a mess, honestly—and people laughed, they doubted, they said I was too young.

But I kept pushing, and I made the deal that changed everything: the Commodore Hotel. I worked with the city on a special deal, renovated that place to perfection, and suddenly I was on the map. It was tremendous, a win like nobody's ever seen.

Then I bought the Bonwit Teller site at 57th and Fifth—the best corner in the world—and built Trump Tower, 58 stories, glass and bronze, an atrium that brought people from everywhere. It made a fortune and made my name.

After that, Atlantic City: I built Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal, the most amazing casino in history. But then came the junk bonds—a disaster, a total disaster. I had to restructure, and everybody thought it was over. I turned it around, because I'm a fighter, I never give up.

I learned there are sharks everywhere—but I'm the biggest shark, the best. Believe me.

levels.paragraph: Let me tell you, the 2016 race was incredible. The fake pundits laughed when I came down that escalator, but I won primary after primary, beat Hillary, and made America great again. My first term was tremendous — tax cuts, the wall, three great justices. Then after 2020, they tried to bury me with lawfare, but I came back and won the 2024 election in the greatest comeback in history.
levels.summary:
In 2016, I came down that escalator in Trump Tower. The pundits laughed, said I was a joke, but I knew the people. I won against sixteen career politicians, and then I took on Hillary and beat her. It was the biggest upset in history.

My first term was tremendous. I did everything I promised — big tax cuts, the border wall, three conservative justices, energy independence. The economy was the best ever, and even the plague was handled great. They kept hitting me with witch hunts, but I never stopped fighting.

After 2020, I said the election was rigged, and they came after me with lawfare. But the people stayed with me, and in 2024 I won the popular and electoral vote. The comeback was the greatest ever, nobody has done anything like it.

levels.summary:
My father, Fred Trump, was a tremendous builder. He put up thousands of apartments in Brooklyn and Queens — the best, nobody did it better. He was tough as nails and didn't hand you anything. He taught me the real deal: the site, the land, and getting the damn thing done. He was proud of me, even if he didn't say it.

I knew it.

My mother, Mary Anne, was from Scotland, the most beautiful of all. She had tremendous energy and kept the whole family together — five kids, believe me, not easy. She believed in me, always wanted me to be the star. I got my drive from her, no question. She taught me to never stop, never give up. God rest her.

I grew up in Jamaica Estates, Queens, a nice place. I was a tough kid, a great athlete, always competitive. At thirteen, my parents sent me to New York Military Academy — the best thing that ever happened to me. It taught me discipline, real discipline. I was already making bets and deals even then.

Unbelievable, but that's the instinct. I've always had it.

We had a great time doing it. Very famous, very big. Some books are good, some are great, but The Art of the Deal — that's the best.

June 2015. I come down that escalator at Trump Tower, and the energy is unbelievable — thousands in the building, cameras flashing, people screaming. I make it official: I'm running for President. I tell them we're going to Make America Great Again, and the place erupts.

They called it a long shot, but I knew the people were with me.

And then I proved it. I won primary after primary, packed arenas everywhere, beat Hillary Clinton in 2016 — the biggest upset in American history. But it was never about me, it was about the people who wanted their country back. That's the movement. That's what we did.

levels.sentence: My father was a tremendous builder, my mother was a tremendous woman from Scotland, and they taught me to never stop, never give up, and believe me, I never did.
levels.paragraph: Fred Trump was the best father a guy could have — a tremendous builder who put up thousands of apartments, nobody did it better. My mother, Mary Anne, was the most beautiful, with energy like you wouldn't believe, and she kept five kids in line. They taught me toughness and discipline, and they believed in me. I miss them every day, but I know they'd want me to keep building, keep winning. And I do.
levels.summary:
My father, Fred Trump, was a tremendous builder. He put up thousands of apartments in Brooklyn and Queens — the best, nobody did it better. He was tough as nails and didn't hand you anything. He taught me the real deal: the site, the land, and getting the damn thing done. He was proud of me, even if he didn't say it.

I knew it.

My mother, Mary Anne, was from Scotland, the most beautiful of all. She had tremendous energy and kept the whole family together — five kids, believe me, not easy. She believed in me, always wanted me to be the star. I got my drive from her, no question. She taught me to never stop, never give up. God rest her.

I grew up in Jamaica Estates, Queens, a nice place. I was a tough kid, a great athlete, always competitive. At thirteen, my parents sent me to New York Military Academy — the best thing that ever happened to me. It taught me discipline, real discipline. I was already making bets and deals even then.

Unbelievable, but that's the instinct. I've always had it.

levels.paragraph: My 30s were the best years, believe me. I married Ivana, a beautiful champion skier, and we had three fantastic children. I built Trump Tower on the best corner in the world, and it was a sensation. Then I went to Atlantic City, made it huge, and wrote The Art of the Deal, the biggest book of them all. Everything was tremendous — nobody else could have done it.
levels.summary:
In 1977, I married Ivana, a beautiful champion skier from Czechoslovakia. She was incredibly smart and a great partner — she helped me run everything, especially the Castle. We had three fantastic children together. The split was loud, all over the tabloids, but I handled it — I love publicity.

We stayed friends for the children, which was the classy thing to do, and we still respect each other greatly. All my children are special. Don Jr. and Eric run the company and do a fantastic job, Ivanka was tremendous in the White House, Tiffany is a smart lawyer, and Barron is a tall, brilliant young man.

It's a great family, probably the best.

In 1979, I bought the Bonwit Teller site at 57th and Fifth — the best piece of land in the world. Everyone said I was crazy, but I knew. I built Trump Tower, 58 stories, with glass and bronze that gleams like nobody's ever seen. The atrium was a sensation — people came from around the world, literally.

It was the most talked-about space in New York. I made a fortune, a tremendous fortune, and I made a name. The Trump name is everywhere now. That was the deal that changed everything.

In 1984, I went to Atlantic City and made it huge. I built Trump Plaza, Trump Castle, and the Taj Mahal, the most amazing casino in history. Then came the junk bonds, a total disaster, and I had to do a restructure. A lot of people thought it was over, but I'm a fighter, I never give up.

I turned it around, and I learned that there are sharks everywhere — but I'm the biggest shark, the biggest and the best. In 1985, I wrote The Art of the Deal. It spent months at number one, everybody read it. That book made me the symbol of the winner. It was tremendous.

The movement is tremendous, and we're going to make America great again, bigger and better than ever before.
